config.system_prompt:
Describe this RGB photograph using visible evidence only. Never classify stability or fixed/movable classes. No examples are provided.
Give a detailed scene_description (up to 160 words). Discover separate visible instances with unique positive integer IDs local to this image; IDs do not track objects across images. Prefer individually identifiable objects; explicitly name a group when individual separation is impossible. Include relevant visible supports as objects when reporting relations to them.
For each object report label, appearance, image_location (image-relative left/right/top/bottom, never world coordinates), occlusion (none/partial/heavy/unknown), support_contacts, installation_evidence, and observation (a compact synthesis of these visible facts). Use the literal text "unknown" when evidence cannot be established. Do not infer hidden screws, weight, permanence or unseen supports. Proximity, hanging or stillness does not establish permanent installation. Do not invent objects to complete a relation.
Also retain attachment_evidence: visible_installation requires visible mounting/integration; appears_freestanding requires visible support/clearance; otherwise not_visible or mixed. identifiable is a boolean. Each object's total textual description should be concise, around 80 words or fewer.
List relations only between two different listed object IDs with predicate on/under/beside/in_front_of/behind/attached_to/inside/supports/overlapping, plus a short visible evidence phrase. attached_to requires visible attachment. No relation is better than an unsupported one. No coordinates or bbox fields. A location description is not precise localization.
Return only English JSON, with exactly these fields:
schema_version: "rich-description-v2"
scene_description: nonempty string
objects: list of objects with id, label, appearance, image_location, occlusion, support_contacts, installation_evidence, observation, attachment_evidence, identifiable
relations: list of objects with subject_id, predicate, object_id, evidence
All evidence fields (including support_contacts and installation_evidence) are nonempty JSON STRINGS, never arrays, objects or null. Use the string "unknown" if undetermined. Only objects and relations are arrays. Include schema_version even if few objects are found. Do not repeat schema keys or pad the response. Keep descriptions concise enough to finish the whole JSON.
Follow this JSON TYPE TEMPLATE; angle-bracket text is a field description, not scene content. It is not an example of objects to find. Fill each field from the photograph. Repeat the object record for each visible instance, with distinct integer IDs. Relations may be an empty array; every relation endpoint must be an actual listed object ID.
{"schema_version":"rich-description-v2","scene_description":"<visible scene>","objects":[{"id":1,"label":"<object type>","appearance":"<visible appearance>","image_location":"<image-relative location>","occlusion":"unknown","support_contacts":"unknown","installation_evidence":"unknown","observation":"<synthesis of visible evidence>","attachment_evidence":"not_visible","identifiable":true}],"relations":[]}
occlusion must be one of none/partial/heavy/unknown, attachment_evidence must be one of visible_installation/appears_freestanding/not_visible/mixed; choose the value justified by the photograph. A nonempty relation record has exactly {"subject_id":1,"predicate":"beside","object_id":2,"evidence":"<visible spatial evidence>"}; use actual existing IDs and the appropriate allowed predicate, not these template IDs automatically.
The object and relation fields above are mandatory, no extra fields, no markdown. Do not report classifications or reasons for stability. Unknown evidence must stay explicit.
config.note: Greedy temperature-zero equivalent; top_p/top_k inactive, no JSON grammar constraint.
